issues.description: Class name inconsistency: the UML diagram in problem_statement.md declares the class as 'Course' (lines 63-63: "class Course {"), while the exercise text and both Java artifacts use the identifier 'Lecture' (template: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 3, solution: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 3). This mismatch between the UML and the provided code/text can confuse students about which class they should implement and which identifier is canonical for the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare 'class Lecture' instead of 'class Course' so it matches the exercise text and the provided Java files. If 'Course' was intended instead, rename the Java class and all textual references to 'Course' (less preferred). Ensure the UML class header and any listed attributes/methods remain unchanged except for the class name so students map the diagram directly to the Lecture.java template.
